abstract: Arising from many applications at the intersection of decision-making and machine learning, Marginal Maximum A Posteriori (Marginal MAP) problems unify the two main classes of inference, namely maximization (optimization) and marginal inference (counting), and are believed to have higher complexity than both of them. We propose XOR MMAP, a novel approach to solve the Marginal MAP problem, which represents the intractable counting subproblem with queries to NP oracles, subject to additional parity constraints. XOR MMAP provides a constant factor approximation to the Marginal MAP problem, by encoding it as a single optimization in a polynomial size of the original problem. We evaluate our approach in several machine learning and decision-making applications, and show that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art Marginal MAP solvers.

summary.idea: XOR MMAP replaces the difficult counting component with constrained queries to optimization or satisfiability-style oracles. Added parity constraints support a compact reformulation of the overall problem.
summary.limitations: A polynomial-size encoding does not imply that its oracle calls are easy to solve. The abstract does not state the approximation constant, runtime figures, or application-specific performance.
summary.problem: Some probabilistic decisions require maximizing over choices while summing over uncertain hidden outcomes. This combination, called marginal MAP, can be harder than either operation alone.
summary.results: The paper establishes a constant-factor approximation through an optimization encoding of polynomial size. Evaluations in several decision-making and machine-learning applications outperform multiple existing marginal MAP solvers.
summary.tldr: Use parity-constrained oracle queries to approximate decisions that combine optimization with probabilistic counting.

title: Solving Marginal MAP Problems with NP Oracles and Parity Constraints
